pages.x: Russia and Japan both wanted Korea and Manchuria. Russia had built a railway across Siberia and leased the ice-free harbour of Port Arthur from China. When talks failed, in February 1904, Japan attacked the Russian fleet at Port Arthur by night, before it declared war.

Japanese armies besieged Port Arthur for five months, charging uphill into machine guns and barbed wire, a foretaste of the First World War. Tens of thousands were killed or wounded before the fortress surrendered on 2 January 1905.
In March 1905 the Japanese beat the main Russian army at Mukden in Manchuria, in one of the biggest battles the world had yet seen, with over half a million men. Both sides were exhausted.

Russia sent its Baltic Fleet halfway around the world to save the war. On the way, jumpy officers fired on British fishing boats in the North Sea, taking them for Japanese torpedo boats. Its biggest ships sailed around Africa, and the fleet took seven months to reach Asia.

On 27 May 1905, in the Tsushima Strait between Korea and Japan, Admiral Tōgō Heihachirō's fleet crossed in front of the Russian line and destroyed it. In two days 21 Russian ships were sunk and most of the rest taken; Japan lost three torpedo boats. It was one of the most complete victories in naval history.

At home Russia was in uproar. In January 1905 troops in St Petersburg fired on a peaceful crowd of workers carrying icons and a petition to the tsar, killing hundreds on Bloody Sunday. Strikes, mutinies like that on the battleship Potemkin and peasant risings forced Nicholas II to grant a parliament.

Both empires were nearly broke. President Theodore Roosevelt brought them to talks at Portsmouth, New Hampshire, where in September 1905 Russia gave Japan Port Arthur, half the island of Sakhalin and a free hand in Korea. Roosevelt won the Nobel Peace Prize for it, the first American to win a Nobel Prize.

Japan's victory astonished the world. It made Japan a great power, which took Korea as a colony in 1910, and it inspired people from India to Egypt, who saw that Europeans could be beaten. In Russia, defeat and the revolution of 1905 were a rehearsal for the revolution of 1917.
